documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing well through the winter. Has been out ice fishing a couple of times, dressed warm. No cough, fevers. Back on SS TMP-SMX since November. Transplant visit in December fine per pt.
Meds: tacrolimus 3 BID, mycophenolate 750 BID, prednisone 5, TMP-SMX SS, lithium 300 BID, amlodipine 10, HCTZ 25.
O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Graft nontender. No edema.
A/P: s/p re-transplant with treated rejection and treated PJP, now well. HTN at goal. Bipolar stable. BMP/CBC today. RTC 4 months.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts and kidney function look stable, right where they have been. Nothing new to do.

documents.title: Outpatient psychiatry letter
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outside psychiatry practice.
Seen for routine review. Euthymic through a hard autumn with his pneumonia admission. No hypomanic or depressive symptoms, sleep regular. Lithium levels with transplant labs in range. Continue lithium carbonate 300 mg BID.
Dx: bipolar I disorder, in remission. Allergies: NKDA. Return 6 months.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe. The remaining lungs are clear. No effusion. Heart size normal.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: Multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after IV gadolinium. Solitary ring-enhancing lesion in the frontal lobe. No other enhancing lesion. Ventricles normal in size. No midline shift. No hemorrhage.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of visit 04/17/2023.

CC: ten days of cough that keeps getting worse, fevers, losing weight.
HPI: 57-year-old kidney transplant recipient with Pneumocystis pneumonia last fall. Besides the cough he has had a dull headache for about a week and some trouble keeping his focus. No recent travel or sick contacts. Taking his immunosuppression as prescribed, tacrolimus and prednisone included.
Meds: tacrolimus 3 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, TMP-SMX SS daily, lithium 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father hypertension and CKD; sister bipolar disorder; maternal uncle ESRD.
Social: does not smoke (quit years ago); no recent travel or known sick contacts.

Vitals: T 38.4 C (101.1 F), RR 22, HR 96, BP 128/80, SpO2 95% RA.
Exam: crackles over the right upper lobe. Neuro exam nonfocal.

Sputum Gram stain: branching gram-positive rods, Nocardia.
CXR: cavitary right upper lobe lesion.
MRI brain: single ring-enhancing lesion, frontal lobe.

Impression: nocardiosis involving lung and brain. Admitted; ID and transplant consulted.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service. Admitted 04/17/2023, discharged 05/01/2023.

Diagnosis: nocardiosis, pulmonary and central nervous system.
Course: IV trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (high dose, renally adjusted) and IV imipenem started on admission. Sputum culture final 04/24: Nocardia species. Neurosurgery reviewed the MRI; with a sputum diagnosis and a small single lesion, medical treatment with serial imaging was chosen, no aspiration. Headache resolved by day 5, fevers by day 4. Creatinine and potassium watched daily, stable. Transplant continued tacrolimus 3 mg BID and mycophenolate.
After 2 weeks of IV therapy transitioned to oral TMP-SMX DS 2 tablets twice daily, planned for 12 months total given brain involvement; this replaces his daily prophylactic tablet.
Discharge medications: TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs BID; tacrolimus 3 mg BID; mycophenolate 750 mg BID; prednisone 5 mg daily; lithium 300 mg BID; amlodipine 10 mg; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: infectious disease 6 weeks with repeat brain MRI; primary care 1 week; weekly BMP and CBC for a month.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharged 5/1 after two weeks for nocardia in the lung and a small brain lesion.
S: Headache gone, thinking clear, wife agrees he is himself. Cough mostly gone. Appetite coming back; down to 81 kg from 86. No fever. Taking TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs twice a day, plenty of water.
O: Weight 81 kg. Vitals as charted, afebrile. Lungs: faint crackles R upper field. Neuro: alert, oriented, fluent, strength and gait normal.
Records reviewed and med list reconciled (SS prophylaxis replaced by the treatment course).
A/P
1. Nocardiosis, lung and brain: 12-month oral course, ID follow-up with MRI in June/July. Weekly BMP/CBC; drawn today.
2. Weight loss from the illness: high-calorie foods, recheck weight next visit.
3. Driving: hold until ID/neurosurgery say otherwise; he agreed, wife is driving.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: A whole year?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Is it right that I need to take these big antibiotic pills for a whole year? That seems like a lot. I feel fine now.

documents.title: RE: A whole year?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, that is the standard length when nocardia has reached the brain, especially with a transplant, because it can come back if stopped early. Infectious disease will follow your MRI and decide the stop date. Keep your labs going so we can watch your kidney and potassium on the higher dose.

reports.study: MRI brain with and without contrast
reports.text: Comparison 04/17/2023. The ring-enhancing frontal lobe lesion is smaller, with less surrounding signal change. No new lesion. Ventricles normal.
reports.conclusion: Interval decrease of the frontal lobe lesion.

documents.title: Infectious disease clinic letter
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outpatient infectious disease. Visit 07/14/2023.
Nocardiosis of lung and brain in a kidney recipient, on oral TMP-SMX DS 2 tablets twice daily since 05/01.
Feels well, cough resolved, no headache. No rash. Labs from primary care and transplant reviewed: counts and potassium acceptable.
Repeat brain MRI 07/11: frontal lesion smaller, nothing new.
Plan: continue the same dose to complete 12 months (end of April 2024). Repeat MRI near the end of therapy. OK to resume driving.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Feels good. Driving again since ID cleared him. Back on the water early mornings. Gaining weight back. Tolerating TMP-SMX DS 2 BID.
O: Weight up, vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Neuro normal. No edema.
PHQ-9: 3.
A/P: nocardiosis improving on therapy (MRI smaller in July), HTN at goal, bipolar stable. Continue all. Flu/COVID vaccines this autumn. RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary (ICU and medicine)
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital. Admitted via the emergency department to the medical ICU 10/15/2023; transferred to medicine 10/19; discharged 10/31/2023.

Presentation: 58-year-old kidney recipient, history of Pneumocystis pneumonia (2022) and nocardiosis of lung and brain (04/2023, on oral TMP-SMX), brought in by his wife after one day of fever and neck pain. Temperature 103 F (39.4 C) on arrival, HR 108. Neck stiff and painful to flex.
Meds on admission: tacrolimus 3 mg BID, mycophenolate 750 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg, TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs BID, lithium 300 mg BID, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father hypertension and CKD; sister bipolar disorder; maternal uncle ESRD.
Social: former smoker, quit about 7 years ago; no alcohol; retired postal worker.

Workup: lumbar puncture with opening pressure 31 cm H2O. CSF cryptococcal antigen positive, titer 1:640; CSF fungal culture grew Cryptococcus neoformans. Serum cryptococcal antigen positive.

Diagnosis: cryptococcal meningitis.
Course: induction with liposomal amphotericin B and flucytosine for 14 days (completed 10/28), with daily creatinine and electrolytes; IV fluids with each amphotericin dose. Two further therapeutic lumbar punctures on days 2 and 4 for raised pressure; headache and neck pain settled. Fever resolved by day 5. ICU for the first four days for neuro checks, never intubated. Transplant service lowered tacrolimus to 2 mg BID ahead of fluconazole.

Discharge medications: fluconazole 400 mg daily for 8 weeks (consolidation), then ID to set maintenance; tacrolimus 2 mg BID; mycophenolate 750 mg BID; prednisone 5 mg daily; TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs BID (nocardia course continues); lithium 300 mg BID; amlodipine 10 mg; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg.
Follow-up: ID 4-6 weeks, transplant 1 week with tacrolimus level, primary care 1 week.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home since 10/31 after cryptococcal meningitis: ICU 4 days, two weeks of amphotericin and flucytosine.
S: Tired but improving daily. No headache, neck pain gone, no fever. Wife giving him his pill box. Taking fluconazole 400 daily, tacrolimus now 2 mg BID (transplant drew a level yesterday), TMP-SMX DS 2 BID, rest unchanged.
O: Vitals as charted, afebrile. Alert, oriented, conversation normal. Neck supple. Gait steady. No edema.
Discharge summary reviewed, list reconciled (tacrolimus 2 BID, fluconazole added).
A/P
1. Cryptococcal meningitis, after induction: fluconazole consolidation 8 wk; ID follow-up booked.
2. Nocardiosis: continues oral course.
3. Electrolytes after amphotericin: BMP and magnesium today.
4. Third opportunistic infection in a year; asked transplant whether his overall immunosuppression should be revisited, they will review.
RTC 3 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Nurse Visit: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Three weeks out from hospital, feeling stronger, afebrile. ID said fine to vaccinate. Flu R deltoid, updated COVID L deltoid. No reaction.

medications.reason: consolidation complete; step down to maintenance

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (200 mg) by mouth daily for 12 months

documents.title: Infectious disease clinic letter
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Outpatient infectious disease. Visit 12/22/2023.
Cryptococcal meningitis (10/2023) after induction and 8 weeks of fluconazole 400 mg; no headache, no fever, cognition back to baseline per wife. Nocardiosis: on TMP-SMX DS 2 tabs BID through April.
Plan: fluconazole down to 200 mg daily from 12/25 as maintenance for 12 months. Transplant aware; tacrolimus stays at 2 mg BID while he is on fluconazole, levels per transplant.
Allergies: NKDA. Return in 4 months with brain MRI.
